text: And the two halves of the record are very different. From nineteen fifty-four to nineteen eighty, the Treasury bill rate mostly climbed, in waves. It peaked at sixteen point three percent in May nineteen eighty-one, then mostly drifted down over the following decades, with big swings. Same loan, same head start; the only difference is where in history it began. Loans started in the climbing years often met rates that rose early and stayed high, and loans started after the peak mostly rode rates down. The best stretch began in August nineteen eighty-one, near that peak, and cost fifteen thousand two hundred ninety-five dollars less than the fixed loan. It belongs to the falling half, while the worst, April nineteen seventy-seven, belongs to the climbing half, where far more of Leah's stretches cost more.
